text: “My order is late. Can I claim compensation?”

A clear explanation
and a next step

Enough context
to decide and respond
Service breaks when facts or context fail to reach the decision-maker.
Historical sample: 546,364 non-prebooked orders; 14.8% late; 1.4% >10 min.

Meituan INFORMS TSL, 17–24 Oct 2022; delivery-delay shares, not complaint rates.
This research was supported by data provided by Meituan.
notes:
A late-delivery complaint needs an identified order, verified ownership and timing, and enough context for human review. The historical Meituan INFORMS TSL research sample covers 17–24 Oct 2022. Team aggregates contain 546,364 non-prebooked delivered orders with a promised time. 14.78% were late and 1.41% were more than 10 minutes late, shown as 14.8% and 1.4%. These figures describe delivery delay in a historical research sample, not complaint rates or current platform-wide performance.

Source: https://github.com/meituan/Meituan-INFORMS-TSL-Research-Challenge ; team aggregates work/data/meituan_lateness_stats.json. Lateness is actual arrival minus promised arrival; one delivered waybill is retained per order.
This research was supported by data provided by Meituan.

text: Missing facts or a dispute: explain the reason, preserve context and route to human service.
notes:
Workflow: understand the request, verify ownership and order facts, evaluate the rule, obtain customer confirmation, review and display the stored result. Reconsideration applies to rejected, uncompensated tickets with verifiable new information or a prior error, a recorded reason and the original ticket. R002 can change the integer amount within 1–20 yuan and the paid-amount cap. Each order has one successful compensation.

text: LangChain connects model/tools. LangGraph manages state and human waits.

Demo: DeepSeek Flash — low-cost model already integrated with order tools.
Formal: GPT-5.6 Sol — available API with native tool calls and per-request usage logs.
Formal settings: T=0.35 · 800 output tokens · 30 s timeout · no retries · code 176fbb0
notes:
LangChain connects model and tools; LangGraph manages state and human waits. The demo reuses the working DeepSeek Flash tool-calling implementation at low reported development/demo cost (developer estimate CNY1–5). Formal B/C runs use the owner-selected GPT-5.6 Sol API with identical settings, complete response/usage logs and fixed code 176fbb0. Formal settings: reasoning none, temperature 0.35, 800 output tokens, 30-second timeout, zero retries; automatic approval disabled. C also has intent handling, order-number fallback and food-safety preprocessing, so results compare configured systems.

Source: examples/ord001/evidence/gpt56-formal-20261123/profile.json and the developer runtime/cost intake. No cross-model selection benchmark was performed.

text: Fix observed failures first · 120 real-model trials on synthetic orders

B: 14 false blocks
6 unclear next steps
3 unwanted cards

C: 9 goodwill cases pending
Retest affected paths
PROPOSED ROLLOUT · FUTURE STAGES AND RELEASE GATES

Gate: policy decided;
affected paths pass.

Few real orders;
human approval retained.

Gate: no wrong / duplicate
issues; review checks pass.

Increase volume;
monitor and roll back.
Later: e-commerce after-sales, with new connectors and revalidated policies.
notes:
The proposed rollout follows repairs to the observed defects: B has 14 amount-mention false blocks, 6 unclear next steps and 3 unwanted confirmation cards; C has 6 unsupported reminder/relay promises and 9 goodwill-policy cases pending. Resolve the policy and retest affected paths first.

Stage 1, shadow mode: produce read-only suggestions while humans decide. Release gate: the pending policy is decided and affected regression paths pass.
Stage 2, limited pilot: use a small set of authorized real orders only after production interfaces are validated; human approval remains required. Release gate: no wrong or duplicate issues in the pilot and human review checks pass.
Stage 3, gradual scaling: increase volume with monitoring and rollback. Release gate: measured net time savings after review/rework and a positive value case under local costs.

These are proposed future stages. Later e-commerce transfer needs new connectors and revalidated policies. Source: work/eval/gpt56-complete-review-2026-11-23.md; rollout gates are project recommendations.
